The mechanism is confirmed: in the steady proxy, E keeps 88-94% of the heap on huge pages against 49% with jemalloc defaults, with -60% dTLB misses, -46% page faults and -2.2% engine time. Exactness: until the loop's first act it writes only liquidation-CF rows (cooldown/pending), which liq_view never reads. From the first act on, the remaining pre-values are dropped and every account is valued live (the 29bfc705 path). An Err from a pre-value is returned at the same trader, after the same earlier writes. A panicking pool job falls back to the live path. The memo entries the pool creates hold the same values whoever builds them. One residual difference: on a storage READ fault, a pre-valued trader past the act cut could record the fault first; that is a fail-stop on either path.
Node expectation: the step costs 3.57 ms/blk; a 65-75% cut saves ~2.3-2.7 ms/blk on the exec thread, about +4-6% blk/s if exec-bound. Risk: 3 validators share 32 threads and run the step at about the same time, so the pool speedup in the node may be lower; only a cell can show this.

The serial loop stops at the act cap (LIQ_ACT_PER_BLOCK=64) or at an early Err, so some candidates it would never value with the flag off still get valued. Their reads can latch ctx.reader_fault, a OnceLock. The only way that happens on this path is AccountReader::mark (native_executor.rs:2924-2931 via sums_of :3171) doing usable_mark for a market outside the block mark table, or for any market when fill_block_marks did not build the table. take_fatal_error (:7266) then fails the block, where with the flag off the block would have committed. This needs a local storage read or decode fault, so it is node-local and fail-stop (no wrong state, no digest risk). Still, it breaks the 'exact' claim, and the report's line 'a fail-stop condition on either path' is wrong. Fix: in liquidation_pass (it holds &mut ctx), record `let had = ctx.reader_fault.get().is_some()` before the pass. If after the pass `!had && ctx.reader_fault.get().is_some()`, call `ctx.reader_fault.take()` and set `pre = None`, so the loop runs fully live (the 29bfc705 path) and latches the same fault again only if it reaches that trader. Add a fault-injection test with a faulting read past the act cap: flag on and off must give the same fatal/no-fatal outcome.

Perf claim to correct (report section 6): 'pre-values after an early act are wasted work on the pool, never on the exec thread' is wrong for latency. run_jobs blocks the exec thread for the whole pass before the serial loop starts. If an account near the start of the window acts (a liquidation storm), the entire pass is overhead on top of the full live loop. That is bounded at about the pass's wall time, roughly 1 ms per block at ubench scale, and only in rare act-heavy blocks. An optional mitigation is to skip the pass when pending or cooldown liquidation rows exist (liquidation_due already checks these), but that is not needed for the cell.

After an outlier or adversarial burst the capacities ratchet and stay forever: several GB for the position caches alone, and every later clear() costs O(capacity) on the exec thread. Needs a byte budget, or a drop when capacity is much larger than the last len.

Production fix (Codex P2): the MAKER_FREE clear-in-place (native_executor.rs:3111) has no size cap, so each pool worker keeps its high-water maker map. Apply the same oversize-drop rule as the core lists.

memo_expiry gives exact bounds: a submission still counts while now - ts <= window, and a row goes stale when now - ts > max_age, so the expiry is ts+window+1 / ts+max_age+1, and staleness can only move one way.

- A different set of listed markets, a different stake set, or a different extra market set in the mark table.

issues: P1, proven: flag on lets an order skip the margin check, and flag-on nodes then disagree with flag-off nodes. p2_cert_one (native_executor.rs:10483 onward) adds up every order the sender placed in the call, including orders the exact path later rejects in validate_order_price or the shape check. Nothing checks the sign of price or quantity. One order with a non-positive limit price (or a negative quantity) makes sum_res negative, so `need` goes negative and the sender is certified. Repro: the sender has 100 available. Order A is a buy for 10 at 30000, 20x, needing 15000 IM. Flag off: insufficient margin. Flag on, with a buy at -1e9 in the same batch: order A is accepted and available goes to about -14900. The -1e9 order is rejected with Price in both arms.

P1, proven: flag on (also probe and shadow) panics in consensus execution. In the C_ub loop, `adverse = if p.is_buy { base - r } else { r - base }` uses FixedPoint Sub, which calls expect() and panics on overflow. A batch with [sell 1 @ mark, sell 1 @ raw i128::MIN+1] in a marked, banded market gives 'FixedPoint subtraction underflow' (torus-types/src/lib.rs:248). Flag off just rejects the second order (Price). Both P1 inputs are stopped by the RPC intake check (order_price_violation plus shape) but not by block execution. So a byzantine proposer, or any ingress that skips the RPC check, can crash or fork flag-on nodes. Fix for both: in pass 1, return NOT_ELIGIBLE unless validate_order_price(p).is_ok() && p.quantity > 0. Also use checked_sub mapped to OVERFLOW for both adverse terms. Then add the two review probe tests to p2_cert_tests.rs, with a shadow run.

P2 (Codex): the certificate only runs in the serial Phase-2 loop. On the sharded path (TORUS_PARALLEL_ENGINE >= 2 and >= 64 orders) prepare_one gets certified=false, so TORUS_S80_P2_CERT=1 silently does nothing there. This does not affect correctness. PE is off by default (owner s128) and cell.sh does not set it, so a cell would exercise the serial path. Wire the certificates into the workers, or log or document that the sharded path never certifies.

P3: in p2_cert_market, `tup` falls back to 0 when sell_top_up_price(bid_floor) overflows but a bid_floor exists. U_i then uses max(limit, 0), while prepare_one still floors the reservation at the bid, so R+T is under-counted. Practically unreachable (bid > ~1.7e26 units), but the claimed proof has a hole. Use bid_floor as the fallback, or bail when bid_floor is Some and the top-up price is None.

P3, test weakness: no test puts a certified sender at the bound. The differential fixture certifies only senders with large slack, and the 100M bench balances give about 98.8% minimum slack. So C_ub (pool never binds) is checked empirically, never at the edge. Also, no test mixes invalid orders (non-positive price, quantity below the lot, band or shape rejects) into a certified sender, which is exactly where the P1 bugs are. perf_equivalence_golden mostly bails (unmarked markets), so it gives little coverage of the skip path.

P3: the cfg(test) global sticky P2_CERT_SKIPPED stays true for the rest of the test process, which turns off match_setup's M1 `pre_pos.is_none()` mismatch check. Under `cargo test`, which runs threads in one process, this weakens the M1 oracle for unrelated tests. Use a thread-local, or per-sender tracking instead.

P3, operational: `ub` mode is unsound by design, and `shadow` uses a release assert! that panics a node when a check fails. Neither may ever run on a validator. Remove or compile-gate both before this goes past prototype.
